_comment: rebalance_app: Harvey, Mazzoleni and Melone, 'The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing' (NBER w33554, February 2025). Pension and target-date funds hold about 60% stocks / 40% bonds and rebalance at month ends, so when stocks have run ahead of bonds that month, stocks fall against bonds in the month's last days (about 17bp a day per standard deviation of the drift), and bounce on the first day of the next. The paper: Sharpe about 1.1 front-running it, 1997 to 2023, stronger since 2006 and 'even stronger' through 2025. Development and validation overlap its sample (a replication, on ETFs instead of futures); the holdout starts when it came out. Fixed 2026-11-15.
_signal_comment: At each close, the stock weight of a portfolio that was target_stock_weight stocks (SPY) and the rest bonds at the last month end, less the target: the drift. Through the month's last window_days trading days, hold the other way to it (positive drift: short stocks against bonds); on the next month's first day (reversal_day), the same way as the drift that set the window. Scaled: a drift of full_at_drift is a whole position (capped there); all in: the direction only. Set at the close, held to the next close (market-on-close orders). Prices include dividends and coupons (adjustment all).
_control_comment: Each variant against random_draws versions of itself with each month's direction decided by a coin (same days, same sizes): the share of them it beat is printed at the end, by period.
_variants_comment: bond: the Treasury fund (IEF 7-10 years, nearest the paper's 10-year note futures; TLT 20+ years). legs: spread (stocks against the bond fund, a whole position being one of each), stocks (SPY alone, long or short), stocks_long_only (SPY only when it's expected to rise). slippage_percent: each fill of each leg.
